claims: Mobileye's Q2 2026 Form 10-Q states that Intel directly or indirectly held approximately 77.1% of Mobileye's outstanding common stock and 96.9% of its voting power as of June 27, 2026.

Mobileye's 2025 Form 10-K describes Intel's ability to control matters submitted to stockholders and identifies additional consent rights over specified major corporate actions while Intel retains at least 20% beneficial ownership.

The same 10-K states that Mobileye qualifies as a Nasdaq controlled company and may rely on exemptions from certain governance requirements, so public Class A holders do not have the same governance protections as holders of companies subject to all Nasdaq corporate-governance requirements.

This evidence supports a bounded governance-risk input for Alpha: economic execution can remain strong while minority-holder influence over board composition and major strategic actions remains structurally limited. It does not establish present abuse, value destruction, or a current conflict.
causalEdges: dual-class voting structure -> Intel 96.9% voting power -> control over stockholder-approved matters -> reduced minority-holder influence
Intel consent rights over specified major actions -> constrained unilateral strategic flexibility -> governance dependency while ownership threshold persists
controlled-company status -> permitted governance exemptions -> fewer mandatory independent-governance protections for Class A holders

risks.risk: Intel's voting control materially exceeds its economic ownership, concentrating decision authority over stockholder matters.
Specified consent rights and controlled-company exemptions can limit minority-holder influence and independent-governance protections without proving any current misuse of that authority.

contradictions: Intel's strategic relationship can provide ecosystem support while the same ownership structure concentrates governance authority; strategic alignment and minority-governance exposure can coexist.
unknowns: This evidence does not establish that Intel currently intends to exercise control in a manner adverse to Mobileye or minority holders.
The durability of the current voting concentration depends on future ownership changes and the dual-class/consent-right framework.
No numeric valuation penalty or risk score is inferred from these governance facts.
falsifiers: A material reduction in Intel voting control or termination of the relevant consent rights would weaken this governance concentration risk.
Governance changes that restore the full Nasdaq independent-governance protections would reduce the controlled-company protection gap.
Evidence that minority holders gain materially greater voting influence over major corporate actions would require reassessment of this structural dependency.
authorityBoundary: Bounded Beta risk-source support only. No Alpha numeric underwriting, numeric risk score, canonical score/rank/tick, root ownership transfer or Chief decision is asserted.
